clues: An embryonic tube that normally disappears in the neck
It marks the path along which a midline gland descends from the base of the tongue
A cyst in the remnant of this tube moves upward when the tongue is stuck out
A migratory cell population that arises from the dorsal part of the neural folds
It gives rise to melanocytes, dorsal root ganglia and much of the facial skeleton
Deficient migration of these cells into the first arch causes Treacher Collins syndrome
An endoderm-lined outpocketing found between the arches
Its derivatives include the thymus and the parathyroid glands
Four pairs form, and the first becomes the middle ear cavity and auditory tube
Paired outgrowths that develop on either side of the developing mouth
They swing from a vertical to a horizontal position and join in the midline
Failure of these to meet leaves a gap in the roof of the mouth
An embryonic rod that guides the early development of the lower face
It gives rise to the malleus and incus
The skeletal rod of the first pharyngeal arch around which the mandible forms
